text:
GENERATE BURST CS-near-canyon — NEAR-CAMERA LAYER SAMPLE: add one foreground object passing close in front of the camera, Hades-style (Matt R-C3-68/79). task_id "CS-near-canyon".

IMAGE 1 (1536×1024) is an in-game frame of a hand-painted 2D ARPG (black bars top and bottom are not part of the game view): a sunset cliffside, the player character standing on the path, a canyon of sunset clouds and a painted valley beyond.
Use image_gen in EDIT mode on IMAGE 1 and deliver ONE 1536×1024 image that is the SAME frame with ONE added near-camera object: a tall weathered SANDSTONE SPIRE (a desert hoodoo: banded red-orange and ochre rock, eroded ledges, a few clinging dry shrubs) rising up out of the canyon clouds in the RIGHT third of the frame, very close to the camera — so it appears LARGE (its base hidden below the bottom edge, its top ending around the upper third of the frame) and it passes IN FRONT of the canyon, cliff and clouds behind it. It is nearer to the camera than the cliff-top ground, so paint it bigger and slightly darker and cooler than the lit scene (in partial silhouette, strong sunset rim light on its upper-left edges), with a very slight softness for depth. It must NOT cover the character or the dirt path near her; it covers at most ~15 % of the frame. Keep everything else exactly as it is, including the character and the black bars. The object is fully painted in the game's hand-painted register (tapered dark contours, painted planes, bold jewel tones).

One image_gen call. ONE retry only if the object covers the character, the rest of the frame was repainted, or the object reads as distant rather than close to the camera — name the reason. Copy the output from $CODEX_HOME/generated_images/... to out/near_canyon.png with sha256. No code. No other files. No web.
RETURN: receipt task_id "CS-near-canyon"; images = the file with prompt, references and elapsed_s; calls_used = the TRUE number of image_gen calls; status; concerns. Never PASS/FAIL.
